title: Prostate Radiotherapy in Metastasized Disease In Accelerated Time
summary: For patients with metastatic prostate cancer, prostate radiotherapy is administered—in accordance with the STAMPEDE and PEACE-1 trials—as 20 fractions over 4 weeks, 6 fractions over 6 weeks, or 74 Gy in 37 fractions. Reducing the total treatment duration represents an attractive option, both economically and for the individual patient. Large randomized Phase III trials have recently demonstrated the safety of this therapy in patients with non-metastatic prostate cancer. We hypothesize that prostate SBRT can be safely delivered to this patient cohort within 1–2 weeks using online adaptive CT-guided radiotherapy.

interventions.name: Definitive CT-based online-adaptive stereotactic radiotherapy of the prostate; total dose to the PTV: 35 Gy in 5 fractions (SD 7 Gy).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	histologically confirmed prostate carcinoma with histological classification according to Gleason score and available PSA value (initial diagnosis < 3 months before study enrolment)
•	Stage IV prostate cancer 
•	ECOG 0-2
•	IPSS < 15
•	Prostate volume < 80 cc
•	patient information and written consent
•	patient’s ability to consent
Exclusion criteria:
•	Previous radiotherapy in the pelvis
•	Previous local therapy of the prostate
•	Simultaneous participation in another clinical study that could influence the results of the respective study
•	Extensive obstructive genitourinary symptoms
